body:
Chief ACK + LANDED, both, at merge efce565. Gate on the merged tree, clean archive export at the pinned grakern: scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck PASS, compileAll PASS, embed-grakern 25, embed-bench 40, codec 95 JVM and 95 JS, features 40 JVM and 40 JS, fixtures 108, exit 0. Trees byte-identical to both candidates. bd-01M15844GFA2WPFG4WFZCSDVZN and bd-01M15ABW5GKR97CEWDQT8YCZM3 CLOSED.

THE P0 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS TONIGHT. embed-grakern was writing a PLAIN ContentAddress over transcript-derived chart checksums into every ProviderCall receipt - a dictionary-attackable surface where an adversary holding a candidate transcript computes the same checksum and confirms a match. We sealed exactly that in embed-core hours ago (contract, privacy, baselines) and then left the JVM structural channel doing it through a different door. That door is now shut, and with it the last KNOWN plain-receipt hole in the library. The path there was worth the time it took: the scout asked before editing, discovered that sensitivity is not reachable at the call site and that ORIGIN CANNOT IMPLY IT - a public fixture and researcher-reviewed participant material can both be Hand - and reported that as a design finding rather than inventing a local workaround. That is why the fix is a construction-time context with no default rather than a guess.

SM4SFT02 gives the Atlas range loading with an integrity story that holds without a full fetch: the prelude is the trusted root, its checksum comes from the manifest rather than from the file, offsets are derived rather than stored, and each block digest binds ordinal and firstRow alongside the bytes so a relocated block is caught.

WHAT I WANT BOTH OF YOU TO NOTICE ABOUT HOW THIS WENT. Neither of you was sent back for a rebase, even though both candidates were built on bases that main had moved past. That was possible because you each reported precisely what your tree contained and what it lacked - the scout naming its six paths and asserting no landed commit touched them, the engineer naming its base SHA - which let me verify disjointness in one command and gate both together in a single run. Compare that with the four attempts the receipt slice needed earlier tonight. The difference was never the code; it was whether the report let me check the claim cheaply.

Remaining P0/P1 on the board: none. Everything open is P2 or P3.
